## Sign conventions

Two, and they are the single most misread thing here. Both are signed on
purpose: an absolute value merges a track that started *early* with one that
started *late*, which are opposite conditions.

| Quantity | Definition | Good when |
|---|---|---|
| `off_s` | `trk_start − ATOT` | **negative** — the track began before wheels-off, so a receiver heard the aircraft on the ground |
| `land_s` | `trk_end − ALDT` | **positive** — the track ran on past touchdown, through taxi-in |

## Measured and estimated aerodromes

An aerodrome is in exactly one tier, decided by **its own** measured share —
`measured_pct`, the percentage of movements on its busier side carrying APDF
milestones. An aerodrome counts as **measured** when
`measured_pct ≥ 50`.

| Tier | Milestones | Capture metrics | Ranked on |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Tier A (measured)** | AOBT, ATOT, ALDT, AIBT — all measured by APDF | yes | `coverage_index` |
| **Tier B (estimated)** | Network Manager — take-off is `AOBT_3 + TAXI_TIME_3`, and `ARVT_3` is that sum plus `FLT_DUR_3`, a model output, not a measured landing | **no** — no in-block time exists outside APDF | `detection_pct` |

Of the 352 aerodromes in the 2026 ranking, 89 are measured; the remaining 263
estimated aerodromes clear the `n_gt ≥ 20` sample-size floor.

::: {.callout-note}
## Why the classification is not `t_source`

A flight's `t_source` is `"apdf"` only when **both** of its ends are covered.
That is the right rule for a metric needing both, and the wrong one for a
statistic cut by aerodrome.

Measured on the 2025 sample: 44,841 flights carry a genuine APDF in-block time,
but only 22,588 are labelled `"apdf"` — the other 22,254 *departed* from an
aerodrome APDF does not cover. Tiering on that label put **26 aerodromes with
20 or more movements into the wrong class despite 99–100% of their arrivals
being measured**, Helsinki and Stuttgart among them, because most of their
traffic arrives from uncovered aerodromes. They would have been ranked on
detection alone with every capture column blank.

The per-endpoint flags `dep_measured` and `arr_measured` carry the answer, and
`t_source` is left untouched so that nothing already published on it moves.
:::

The estimated times were validated against real airport records at median error
0 s, IQR 17 s (take-off) and 25 s (landing) — so they are accurate, and still
not observations. That distinction decides what may be asked of them: an
accurate estimate of a *duration* supports a median taxi-out figure, while an
arrival time reconstructed from two predicted durations supports nothing at
all, because it contains no measurement of the landing. `ARVT_3` in particular
reproduces as
`AOBT_3 + TAXI_TIME_3 + FLT_DUR_3` to within 7 s at the median and 30 s at the
maximum, which is minute-rounding: it carries no information about the landing
beyond what the off-block time and the two model durations already say. The tiers are ranked separately
and never interleaved, because they do not measure the same thing.

## Columns

Side-specific columns carry a `_dep` or `_arr` suffix where both sides define
them. Departures group on `gt_adep`, arrivals on `gt_ades`.

### Counts and detection

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `n_gt_dep`, `n_gt_arr` | ground-truth movements at this aerodrome | flights | ≥ 0 | sample size; every other column is unreliable when this is small. Ranking requires ≥ 20 |
| `n_detected_dep`, `n_detected_arr` | movements with ≥ 1 assigned state vector | flights | `0..n_gt` | |
| `detection_pct_dep`, `detection_pct_arr` | `100 · n_detected / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | 100 = every movement seen at least once. The most basic coverage reading there is |
| `dep_bins_total`, `arr_bins_total` | `ceil(ground phase seconds / 30)` | bins | ≥ 1 | how many 30 s slices the ground phase contains |
| `dep_bins_seen`, `arr_bins_seen` | bins containing at least one position report | bins | `0..total` | |
| `dep_n_samples`, `arr_n_samples` | position reports inside the ground phase | count | ≥ 0 | |
| `n_capture_excluded_dep`, `..._arr` | **measured** movements with `AOBT ≥ ATOT` or `AIBT ≤ ALDT` | flights | ≥ 0 | bad reference data, excluded from capture rather than clipped. An *unmeasured* endpoint is not counted here — it has no capture, which is not the same as an impossible one |
| `measured_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(endpoint measured by APDF) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | `≥ 50` on either side means the aerodrome's ground coverage can be measured |
| `dep_measured`, `arr_measured` | per flight: did APDF supply this endpoint's milestones | bool | — | capture is computed only where true, so a predicted taxi time never becomes a denominator |

`n_gt` counts **all** ground-truth movements while every percentile below is
over **detected** flights only. The asymmetry is deliberate: an undetected
flight has no offset, and the only way to include it in a percentile would be
to invent one.

### Boundary error

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `off_s_p10` … `off_s_p90` | percentiles of `off_s` over detected departures | s | signed | `p90` is the worst-covered decile. A `p50` near zero means the typical track starts at wheels-off — no ground reception |
| `land_s_p10` … `land_s_p90` | percentiles of `land_s` over detected arrivals | s | signed | `p10` is the worst-covered decile |
| `off_abs_p50`, `off_abs_p90` | percentiles of `|off_s|` | s | ≥ 0 | **comparability with the V1 study only.** Do not read as coverage: it merges early and late starts |
| `land_abs_p50`, `land_abs_p90` | percentiles of `|land_s|` | s | ≥ 0 | as above |

### Ground coverage — measured aerodromes only

Raw seconds are not comparable between aerodromes. A median `off_s` of −180 s
is complete coverage at a regional field with a three-minute taxi and about a
seventh of it at a hub with a twenty-minute one. Normalising by the aerodrome's
own ground phase removes that.

**Two different questions, and they disagree.**

::: {.callout-important}
## Spanned is not observed

**Reach** asks how far back the track's *first* position report lies. It was
the original measure and it is too generous: one report at the stand and
nothing again until the runway spans the entire taxi, and scores **1.000**.

**Continuity** asks how much of the taxi was *actually observed*. The ground
phase is cut into 30-second bins and each is asked whether any position report
fell inside it. At the feed's 5-second cadence a bin should hold about six
reports, so an empty bin is a genuine reception gap rather than one dropped
message.

The coverage index uses **continuity**. Reach is kept on every page, because
high reach with low continuity is exactly the signature of the failure
continuity was added to catch.
:::

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dep_continuity_p10` … `p90` | percentiles of `dep_bins_seen / dep_bins_total` over `[AOBT, ATOT]` in 30 s bins, `dep_measured` flights only | fraction | `0..1` | **the headline**: share of the taxi-out actually observed |
| `arr_continuity_p10` … `p90` | the same over `[ALDT, AIBT]` | fraction | `0..1` | share of the taxi-in actually observed |
| `dep_max_gap_median_s` | median longest silence within the taxi-out, counting the lead-in from off-block and the run-out to take-off | s | ≥ 0 | one long gap with otherwise good coverage points at a blind spot rather than weak reception |
| `arr_max_gap_median_s` | the same for taxi-in | s | ≥ 0 | |
| `dep_reach_p10` … `p90` | percentiles of `clip((ATOT − trk_start) / (ATOT − AOBT), 0, 1)` | fraction | `0..1` | diagnostic only — how much of the taxi-out the track *spans* |
| `arr_reach_p10` … `p90` | percentiles of `clip((trk_end − ALDT) / (AIBT − ALDT), 0, 1)` | fraction | `0..1` | diagnostic only |
| `dep_no_ground_pct` | `100 · #(off_s ≥ 0) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share never heard on the ground at all |
| `arr_no_ground_pct` | `100 · #(land_s ≤ 0) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share lost at or before touchdown |
| `dep_full_capture_pct` | `100 · #(dep_continuity ≥ 0.95) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | share whose whole taxi-out was observed, not merely spanned |
| `arr_full_capture_pct` | `100 · #(arr_continuity ≥ 0.95) / n_detected` | % | `0..100` | |
| `taxi_out_median_s` | median `ATOT − AOBT` | s | > 0 | context: why raw seconds differ between aerodromes |
| `taxi_in_median_s` | median `AIBT − ALDT` | s | > 0 | context |

Both reach and continuity are computed **only from measured milestones**. Outside APDF the
denominator would be `TAXI_TIME_3`, NM's *predicted* taxi time, so the fraction
would measure the prediction as much as the reception — and mixing predicted
and measured denominators inside one column makes the ranking incomparable with
itself.

A non-positive ground phase — off-block after take-off, in-block before
landing — is bad reference data, not zero coverage. Those flights are
**excluded** from the capture statistics and counted in `n_capture_excluded`.
Clipping them instead would score them 0 or 1 and silently move the median.

### Segmentation quality

Present so a poor coverage number can be attributed to reception or to the
algorithm rather than guessed at. Every flight falls in exactly one class, and
a flight that is both merged and fragmented counts as **merged** — merging is
the worse failure, and a flight must not improve its class by breaking a second
way.

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `clean_pct_dep`, `clean_pct_arr` | `100 · #(one flight ↔ one track) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | |
| `fragmented_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(one flight → several tracks) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | recoverable downstream — the flight is present in pieces |
| `merged_pct_dep`, `..._arr` | `100 · #(several flights → one track) / n_gt` | % | `0..100` | **unrecoverable** — the other flights simply do not exist in the output |

### The ranking

| Column | Formula | Unit | Domain | Reading |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `coverage_index` | see below | fraction | `0..1` | the expected share of one movement the network captures |
| `rank` | position in the table | — | ≥ 1 | the measured table ranks on `coverage_index`; the all-aerodromes table on `detection_pct` |

### The coverage index, spelled out

Every term in it is defined above, but the formula is worth writing in full
because each part is itself an average of an average.

```
coverage_index  =  (detection_pct / 100)  ×  mean(dep_signal_p50, arr_signal_p50)
```

Reading it left to right:

- **`detection_pct / 100`** — the share of this aerodrome's movements that
  produced at least one position report between take-off and landing,
  expressed as a fraction rather than a percentage. Near 1.0 almost everywhere.
- **`dep_signal_p50`** — take every departure at this aerodrome, work out what
  share of its expected taxi-out reports actually arrived, and take the median
  of those shares. A median, not a mean, so one unusual flight cannot move it.
- **`arr_signal_p50`** — the same for arrivals, over the taxi-in.
- **`mean(...)`** — the two sides averaged, giving one figure for a typical
  ground movement.

So the index is *the chance a flight is seen at all* multiplied by *how much of
its time on the ground is received when it is*. An aerodrome that detects 99%
of its flights but receives nothing on the ground scores near zero — correctly,
because nothing about its surface movements can be derived.

It is **blank**, not zero, where the ground figures cannot be computed. Falling
back to detection alone would rank an aerodrome whose ground coverage is
unknown as though it were well covered.

`coverage_index` is **NaN**, not zero, when no continuity term exists, and
**never falls back to reach** — doing so would silently restore the defect for
exactly the aerodromes where it could not be measured. An estimated-times
aerodrome has no AIBT, and giving it a fabricated capture — zero included —
would rank it below every measured aerodrome for a reason that has nothing to
do with coverage.

Every component stays a visible column so the ranking can be reproduced, or
rejected, on whichever term the reader cares about.
